title.en: The poet, the king and the arch

heading.en: A king, an arch and a fallen crown

hook.en: How can a fruit end up ruling a city? Vikram Seth tells the answer as a comic tale in verse, and it all starts with a badly built arch.

objectives.en: Introduce Vikram Seth and the form of the poem
Describe the king and his order to build an arch

narration.en: How can a fruit end up ruling a city? Vikram Seth tells the answer as a comic tale in verse, and it all starts with a badly built arch.

body.en: Vikram Seth (born 1952) is an Indian poet and novelist, known for works such as "A Suitable Boy" and "The Golden Gate". "The Tale of Melon City" retells an old folk tale as a humorous narrative poem in short, mostly rhyming couplets. Its light, mock-serious tone hides a sharp satire on rulers and their subjects.

Let us map the king and what surrounds him at the start of the tale.

say.en: At the centre is the king, called just and placid, yet ruled by whims.
He orders an arch, and it is built too low.
Riding under it, the king has his crown knocked off.
The builders are the first to be blamed.
The people watch and obey without question.

body.en: The king of the city is described as just and placid, yet he acts on whims. He orders an arch to be built across a main street so that his subjects may be uplifted by the sight. When he rides under it, the arch is too low and knocks off his crown.

points.en: A "just and placid" king: ironic description
Arch built over a thoroughfare for public uplift
The arch is too low: the crown falls off

problem.en: Why did the king order the arch to be built, and what went wrong?

steps.en: Purpose: an arch across the main street to uplift the people who saw it.
Problem: it was built too low.
Result: when the king rode under it, it knocked off his crown.

answer.en: The king ordered an arch across a busy street so that the people would be uplifted by it. It was built too low, and when he rode beneath it, it knocked off his crown, which made him furious.
